```{python}
#| output: asis
# Every number in this report comes from report_data.json, written by bin/envmetag_report_data.py.
# This document only formats it. Figures are emitted as raw HTML blocks: if pandoc parsed the
# inlined plotly.js as markdown, it would need gigabytes of memory.
import html
import json
import statistics

import plotly.graph_objects as go

with open("report_data.json") as handle:
    data = json.load(handle)

RANKS = ["domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"]
SAMPLES = [s["id"] for s in data["samples"]]
run = data["run"]
method = run["assignment_method"] or "SingleM default"

# 15 distinguishable colours for the top taxa; "Other" and "unassigned" have fixed neutrals
PALETTE = [
    "#4c78a8", "#f58518", "#54a24b", "#e45756", "#72b7b2", "#b279a2", "#eeca3b", "#9d755d",
    "#ff9da6", "#79706e", "#2f8f9d", "#bab0ac", "#8cd17d", "#d37295", "#86bcb6",
]
OTHER_COLOUR = "#cbd2d9"
UNASSIGNED_COLOUR = "#52606d"
DOMAIN_COLOURS = {"Bacteria": "#4c78a8", "Archaea": "#f58518"}
FONT = 'system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif'
plotly_js_written = False


def raw(markup):
    print("\n```{=html}\n" + markup + "\n```\n")


def figure(fig):
    global plotly_js_written
    fig.update_layout(template="plotly_white", font={"family": FONT, "size": 13, "color": "#1f2933"},
                      paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)")
    raw('<div class="em-figure">'
        + fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=not plotly_js_written, config={"displaylogo": False})
        + "</div>")
    plotly_js_written = True


def table(header, rows, numeric=()):
    head = "".join(f'<th class="num">{h}</th>' if i in numeric else f"<th>{h}</th>" for i, h in enumerate(header))
    body = "".join(
        "<tr>" + "".join(f'<td class="num">{c}</td>' if i in numeric else f"<td>{c}</td>" for i, c in enumerate(row))
        + "</tr>"
        for row in rows
    )
    return f'<table class="em-table"><thead><tr>{head}</tr></thead><tbody>{body}</tbody></table>'


def lineage_html(lineage):
    # the last field in bold, its ancestors muted
    parts = [html.escape(p) for p in lineage.split(" › ")]
    return '<span class="em-lineage">' + " › ".join(parts[:-1] + [f"<b>{parts[-1]}</b>"]) + "</span>"


deepest = next((r for r in reversed(RANKS) if data["ranks"][r]["available"]), "none")
fractions = [s["read_fraction"] for s in data["samples"]]
genera = {t["taxonomy"] for t in data["ranks"]["genus"].get("taxa", [])} if data["ranks"]["genus"]["available"] else set()
warned = sum(1 for s in data["samples"] if s["warning"])

raw(f'''<div class="em-meta">
  <b>Pipeline</b> ampfalaeris/envmetag {html.escape(run["pipeline_version"])} &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <b>Metapackage</b> {html.escape(run["metapackage"])} &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <b>Assignment</b> {html.escape(method)}
</div>
<div class="em-cards">
  <div class="em-card"><div class="k">Samples</div><div class="v">{len(SAMPLES)}</div>
    <div class="n">{warned} with a SingleM warning</div></div>
  <div class="em-card"><div class="k">Prokaryotic fraction</div><div class="v">{statistics.median(fractions):.1f}%</div>
    <div class="n">median; range {min(fractions):.1f}–{max(fractions):.1f}%</div></div>
  <div class="em-card"><div class="k">Deepest rank assigned</div><div class="v">{deepest.capitalize()}</div>
    <div class="n">across all samples</div></div>
  <div class="em-card"><div class="k">Genera shown</div><div class="v">{len(genera)}</div>
    <div class="n">top {run["top_n"]} by peak abundance</div></div>
</div>''')

links = data["links"]
raw(f'''<div class="em-links em-note">Related reports (relative links; paths shown in case this file was moved):
  <a href="{html.escape(links["multiqc"])}">MultiQC</a> <code>{html.escape(links["multiqc"])}</code> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="{html.escape(links["krona"])}">Krona</a> <code>{html.escape(links["krona"])}</code></div>''')
```

::: {#em-howto .callout-note}
## How to read the numbers

- All abundances are **read-based estimates from SingleM marker genes**. A percentage is a share of **prokaryotic marker-gene coverage**, not a share of reads and not a cell count.
- **Unassigned** is coverage SingleM could not resolve at that rank. It is always shown and never redistributed to named taxa.
- The **prokaryotic fraction** is SingleM's estimate of the share of (fastp-trimmed) read bases from Bacteria and Archaea. The rest may be eukaryotic, viral, host, or unknown. It is a genome-size-based estimate, capped at 100%.
- Presence of a taxon is not evidence that it is active, and not evidence of corrosion or any other process.
:::

## Sample overview

```{python}
#| output: asis
rows = [
    [
        f"<b>{html.escape(s['id'])}</b>",
        f"{s['read_fraction']:.2f}",
        f"{s['average_genome_size_bp'] / 1e6:.2f}",
        f"{s['metagenome_size'] / 1e6:,.1f}",
        (f'<span class="em-badge" tabindex="0" data-tip="{html.escape(s["warning"], quote=True)}" '
         f'aria-label="SingleM warning: {html.escape(s["warning"], quote=True)}">warning</span>')
        if s["warning"] else "",
    ]
    for s in data["samples"]
]
raw(table(["Sample", "Prokaryotic fraction (%)", "Avg. genome (Mbp)", "Read bases (Mbp)", "SingleM"], rows, numeric=(1, 2, 3)))
if warned:
    print('\n<p class="em-note">Hover over (or tab to) a <i>warning</i> badge for SingleM\'s message, shown verbatim.</p>\n')
```

## Community composition

```{python}
#| output: asis
ranks = data["ranks"]
available = [r for r in RANKS if ranks[r]["available"]]
missing = [r for r in RANKS if not ranks[r]["available"]]

print(f"Share of prokaryotic marker-gene coverage per sample (read-based). At each rank, the {run['top_n']} taxa with "
      f"the highest abundance in any one sample have their own colour; the rest are pooled as *Other*. "
      f"Use the menu to change rank; hover for the full lineage.\n")
if missing:
    print(f'\n<p class="em-note">No {", ".join(missing)}-level assignments in this run.</p>\n')
if len(SAMPLES) > run["stacked_bar_max_samples"]:
    print(f"\n*{len(SAMPLES)} samples is more than this layout is designed for "
          f"({run['stacked_bar_max_samples']}); bars may be hard to read.*\n")

fig = go.Figure()
trace_rank = []
for rank in available:
    entry = ranks[rank]
    for i, taxon in enumerate(entry["taxa"]):
        fig.add_bar(
            x=SAMPLES, y=[taxon["values"][s] for s in SAMPLES], name=taxon["label"],
            marker_color=PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)],
            hovertemplate=f"<b>{html.escape(taxon['label'])}</b><br>{html.escape(taxon['lineage'])}"
                          "<br>%{x}: %{y:.2f}%<extra></extra>",
        )
        trace_rank.append(rank)
    if entry["other"] is not None:
        fig.add_bar(
            x=SAMPLES, y=[entry["other"][s] for s in SAMPLES], name=f"Other ({entry['other_count']} taxa)",
            marker_color=OTHER_COLOUR, hovertemplate="<b>Other</b><br>%{x}: %{y:.2f}%<extra></extra>",
        )
        trace_rank.append(rank)
    fig.add_bar(
        x=SAMPLES, y=[entry["unassigned"][s] for s in SAMPLES], name=f"Unassigned at {rank}",
        marker_color=UNASSIGNED_COLOUR, hovertemplate=f"<b>Unassigned at {rank}</b><br>%{{x}}: %{{y:.2f}}%<extra></extra>",
    )
    trace_rank.append(rank)

default_rank = "genus" if "genus" in available else available[-1]
for trace, rank in zip(fig.data, trace_rank):
    trace.visible = rank == default_rank
fig.update_layout(
    barmode="stack", bargap=0.35,
    yaxis={"title": "% of prokaryotic marker-gene coverage", "range": [0, 100.5], "ticksuffix": "%"},
    xaxis={"title": None},
    legend={"title": {"text": "Taxon"}, "traceorder": "normal"},
    height=520, margin={"t": 70, "l": 70, "r": 20, "b": 50},
    updatemenus=[{
        "buttons": [
            {"label": rank.capitalize(), "method": "update", "args": [{"visible": [r == rank for r in trace_rank]}]}
            for rank in available
        ],
        "active": available.index(default_rank),
        "x": 0, "xanchor": "left", "y": 1.14, "yanchor": "top",
        "bgcolor": "#f5f7fa", "bordercolor": "#e4e7eb", "font": {"color": "#1f2933"},
    }],
)
figure(fig)
```

## Taxonomic flow

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"How each sample's coverage divides from domain down to the deepest rank. Band widths are shares of the "
      f"sample's prokaryotic marker-gene coverage (read-based). Taxa below {run['sankey_min_percent']:g}% of a "
      f"sample are pooled into *Other* at their rank; coverage SingleM could not resolve further ends in "
      f"*Unresolved below* the rank where it stopped. Choose a sample from the menu.\n")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| column: page
# Full page width: eight rank columns need more room than the body column. Quarto hides the
# table of contents and the sidebar card while this figure is on screen, so nothing overlaps.


def node_colour(node):
    if node["rank"] == "sample":
        return "#1f2933"
    if not node["lineage"]:
        return UNASSIGNED_COLOUR if node["label"].startswith(("Unresolved", "Unassigned")) else OTHER_COLOUR
    return DOMAIN_COLOURS.get(node["lineage"].split(" › ")[0], "#72b7b2")


SANKEY_LABEL_CHARS = 16  # eight columns share the page width (~105 px each at 11 px text); longer names collide


def short(label, rank):
    # species as "M. maripaludis"; then cut from the middle, since the ending carries the rank
    # (-aceae family, -ales order)
    if rank == "species" and " " in label:
        genus, epithet = label.split(" ", 1)
        label = f"{genus[0]}. {epithet}"
    if len(label) <= SANKEY_LABEL_CHARS:
        return label
    tail = 5
    return label[: SANKEY_LABEL_CHARS - 1 - tail] + "…" + label[-tail:]


def rgba(hex_colour, alpha):
    h = hex_colour.lstrip("#")
    return f"rgba({int(h[0:2], 16)}, {int(h[2:4], 16)}, {int(h[4:6], 16)}, {alpha})"


fig = go.Figure()
for n, sample in enumerate(SAMPLES):
    flows = data["sankey"][sample]
    nodes = flows["nodes"]
    colours = [node_colour(node) for node in nodes]
    fig.add_trace(go.Sankey(
        visible=n == 0,
        arrangement="snap",
        valueformat=".2f", valuesuffix="%",
        node={
            # only taxon names are shortened; "Other …" and "Unresolved …" stay whole
            "label": [short(node["label"], node["rank"]) if node["lineage"] else node["label"] for node in nodes],
            "color": colours,
            "customdata": [f'{node["label"]}<br>{node["lineage"]}' if node["lineage"] else node["label"] for node in nodes],
            "hovertemplate": "%{customdata}<br><b>%{value}</b><extra></extra>",
            "pad": 14, "thickness": 16, "line": {"width": 0},
        },
        link={
            "source": [link["source"] for link in flows["links"]],
            "target": [link["target"] for link in flows["links"]],
            "value": [link["value"] for link in flows["links"]],
            "color": [rgba(colours[link["target"]], 0.35) for link in flows["links"]],
            "customdata": [f'{nodes[link["source"]]["label"]} → {nodes[link["target"]]["label"]}' for link in flows["links"]],
            "hovertemplate": "%{customdata}<br><b>%{value}</b><extra></extra>",
        },
        textfont={"size": 11},
    ))
# height from the most crowded rank column across samples, so stacked nodes keep readable labels
busiest = max(
    max(sum(1 for node in data["sankey"][s]["nodes"] if node["rank"] == rank) for rank in ["sample"] + RANKS)
    for s in SAMPLES
)
fig.update_layout(
    height=max(480, 34 * busiest + 140), margin={"t": 70, "l": 10, "r": 10, "b": 20},
    updatemenus=[{
        "buttons": [
            {"label": sample, "method": "update", "args": [{"visible": [s == sample for s in SAMPLES]}]}
            for sample in SAMPLES
        ],
        "x": 0, "xanchor": "left", "y": 1.13, "yanchor": "top",
        "bgcolor": "#f5f7fa", "bordercolor": "#e4e7eb", "font": {"color": "#1f2933"},
    }],
)
figure(fig)
```

## Taxonomic resolution

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("How far down SingleM resolved each sample: the share of marker-gene coverage whose deepest assignment is at "
      "each rank. Coverage resolved only to a high rank appears as *unassigned* at every rank below it.\n")


def shaded(value):
    # cell background scales with the share, so the resolution profile reads at a glance
    alpha = min(value, 100) / 100 * 0.55
    return (f'<span style="display:block;margin:-.4rem -.6rem;padding:.4rem .6rem;'
            f'background:rgba(var(--em-shade),{alpha:.3f})">{value:.2f}</span>')


levels = data["level_coverage"]
raw(table(
    ["Sample"] + [r.capitalize() + " (%)" for r in RANKS],
    [[f"<b>{html.escape(s)}</b>"] + [shaded(levels[s][r]["relative_abundance"]) for r in RANKS] for s in SAMPLES],
    numeric=tuple(range(1, len(RANKS) + 1)),
))
```

## Per-sample profiles

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("The full SingleM profile of each sample. *Coverage* is SingleM's marker-gene coverage estimate for taxa "
      "assigned exactly at that lineage, not a read count.\n")
for sample in SAMPLES:
    taxa = data["profiles"][sample]
    total = sum(t["coverage"] for t in taxa)
    rows = [[lineage_html(t["lineage"]), f"{t['coverage']:.2f}", f"{t['coverage'] / total * 100:.1f}"] for t in taxa]
    raw(f'<details class="em-profile"><summary>{html.escape(sample)} <span>· {len(taxa)} taxa</span></summary>'
        + table(["Lineage", "Coverage", "Share (%)"], rows, numeric=(1, 2)) + "</details>")
```

## Methods and attribution

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"""
Reads were adapter- and poly-G-trimmed with fastp (no sliding-window quality trimming) and profiled with
SingleM (`singlem pipe`, `prokaryotic_fraction`, `summarise`) against the {html.escape(run['metapackage'])}
metapackage ({html.escape(method)} assignment). PhiX and host reads were removed after profiling, for later
steps; they remain in the prokaryotic-fraction denominator. Tool versions are in the MultiQC report and in
`pipeline_info/envmetag_software_mqc_versions.yml`.

Taxonomy is from the [GlobDB](https://globdb.org) r232 SingleM metapackage, licensed
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Please cite GlobDB
(Speth et al. 2025, doi:10.1093/bioadv/vbaf280) and its [underlying data sources](https://globdb.org/citations),
and SingleM (Woodcroft et al. 2025, doi:10.1038/s41587-025-02738-1).
""")
```
